english: Let $S$ be the set of 13 points consisting of the six vertices of a regular hexagon, the midpoints of its six sides and its centre. The number of triangles whose three vertices belong to $S$ is
hindi: माना कि $S$ उन 13 बिन्दुओं का समुच्चय है जिनमें एक सम षट्भुज के छः शीर्ष, उसकी छः भुजाओं के मध्य-बिन्दु तथा उसका केन्द्र सम्मिलित हैं। उन त्रिभुजों की संख्या, जिनके तीनों शीर्ष $S$ में हैं, है
solution: Each side: vertex, midpoint, vertex $\Rightarrow 6$ triples
Each long diagonal: vertex, centre, opposite vertex $\Rightarrow 3$ triples
Opposite sides are parallel, so their midpoints are symmetric about the centre: midpoint, centre, opposite midpoint $\Rightarrow 3$ triples
No other line contains three points of $S$; collinear triples $=12$, triangles $=286-12=274$
solution_full: Three points of $S$ form a triangle unless they are collinear, so the number of triangles is $\binom{13}{3}$ minus the number of collinear triples; $\binom{13}{3}=286$.
(i) The six sides: each contains two vertices and the midpoint between them, giving 6 triples.
(ii) The three long diagonals: each joins opposite vertices and passes through the centre, giving 3 triples.

(iii) In a regular hexagon opposite sides are parallel and symmetric about the centre $O$, so the midpoints $M$ and $M'$ of opposite sides satisfy $\overrightarrow{OM'}=-\overrightarrow{OM}$; hence $M,O,M'$ are collinear, giving 3 more triples.

No line contains four points of $S$, and no other triple is collinear: the vertices lie on one circle and the midpoints on a smaller concentric circle, so a line meets each circle in at most two points, and the lines through $O$ that contain a vertex or a midpoint are exactly the six lines in (ii) and (iii). A line through a vertex and a midpoint of a non-adjacent side meets no third point of $S$ (direct check with coordinates).
originality_note: New: a 13-point configuration (hexagon vertices, side midpoints, centre) in which the hidden collinearities midpoint-centre-opposite midpoint must be found; the count of lines through three points is the whole difficulty (way 4: a hidden symmetry). Closest known: 'vertices of a regular octagon and its centre: T - S' and 'points on the sides of a triangle'. Different because: three different families of collinear triples occur, one of them not visible from the vertices alone. The first design (12-gon plus centre, T - L) was found on the web as an octagon version and was replaced.
blueprint_concepts: Number of straight lines and triangles formed by points
Number of straight lines, triangles and diagonals from n points

concept_use.Number of straight lines and triangles f: Triangles are C(13,3) minus collinear triples; the triples lie on sides, on long diagonals and on lines through the centre and opposite midpoints.
concept_use.Number of straight lines, triangles and: The long diagonals of the hexagon (diagonals through the centre) and the sides give 9 of the 12 collinear triples; the number of lines and diagonals of the hexagon is what must be examined.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol and object is defined before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed by an independent brute-force enumeration in Python (sympy/itertools), is unique and matches the Answer Plan. Checked with exact coordinates (sympy) that there are exactly 12 collinear triples and no collinear quadruple, and that 274 is at (D) as planned; distractors 280, 277, 283 come from missing one or two of the three families. key_step: Finding all collinear triples, in particular the midpoint-centre-opposite midpoint lines.
justification: Standard formula C(n,3) minus collinear triples, but the configuration has three families of collinear triples, one easy to miss; each distractor is a missed family. Comparable to the lattice-point triangle counting in 2023-P1-Q6 (L3).
